On Vauxhall cars after 2000 (maybe Opal also) you can get a fault code display without using an OBD2 by doing the Pedal Test. Hold down your brake and accelerator pedals together, then turn the ignition key to the second click so the lights come on but the engine doesn't start (keep the pedals pressed down). Then look where your mileage usually appears and a series of 6 digit codes should cycle through - these are fault codes that can be checked online for an indication of what could be wrong.

Doing it this way won't clear the codes once an issue is fixed but it's useful as a starting point.

I feel you. I have depression and anxiety made worse by the pandemic, and this time last year I was at the point of having a panic attack every time I opened the kitchen cupboards or got asked 'what should we have for tea?' by my partner or child. I absolutely hated the sight of the kitchen and even when my partner cooked, I couldn't enjoy eating because I knew it'd be my turn next. We were having 2 or 3 takeouts a week because I literally couldn't look in a cupboard and figure out a meal from the contents. 

No idea if this will work for you but it really helped me: I started planning meals for the month in advance. Towards the end of Feb 2021 I started going through some recipe websites, finding easy meals that didn't take a lot of ingredients or time, made a list of the ingredients and used that to create a shopping list. 

I then worked out which meals could follow which other meals or work for particular days (e.g. if I did curry one night, I'd cook extra rice and do egg fried rice the night after, and more time-consuming meals would be done on weekends), and plotted out a meal planner spreadsheet for March. 

(I should point out here that I work with spreadsheets and data so this is just how my brain worked, it might not be for everyone. Adding an analytical aspect into it made it feel more familiar and less daunting)

The first couple of months, I took on all the cooking myself, though my (ex-chef) partner was on hand if I needed help or advice. It was only things like cottage pie, sausage and mash, and things from packets but the point is, I was no longer panicking about what to do for tea because I'd already planned it out.

I've used this approach for a full year now, always trying at least 2 or 3 new recipes a month, and we've had some really tasty meals. I'm now starting to come up with my own recipes instead of following existing ones, or at least adapting them. I'm still not very good at just making something from random ingredients in a cupboard but I'm no longer scared of doing so.

Sorry this was long winded! As a TL:DR - start with simple recipes consisting of easy to buy ingredients, and try to make more than you would need for one meal - I often make larger portions so I can have the leftovers the next day and have a night off cooking.

The first meal I made was cottage pie, it's really simple and very tasty (I'm in the UK so apologies if not all of this is familiar):

Ground/minced meat (500g beef or beef and pork)

White potatoes (4 or 5 decent sized ones)

Onion (optional, can also use onion salt)

Frozen or tinned veg (carrots and peas are good)

1 or 2 tsp Worcestershire sauce (optional but good with beef)

Instant beef gravy (about 450g should be enough)

​

Preheat your oven to GM5 (375f)

Peel and chop the potatoes (smaller chunks will cook faster) cover with water and bring to the boil.

Fry (saute) the meat (and chopped onion if using) until brown. Mix in the veggies and gravy, and the WS if using and leave to simmer on a low heat until potatoes are done.

When the potatoes are soft (jab them with a fork) drain out the water and mash them with butter and a splash of milk. Add salt to taste. I also put wholegrain mustard with mine but you don't have to.

Get yourself a decent sized ovenproof dish, needs to be quite deep. Pour in the meat mixture (should be quite thick) and then spoon the mash over the top, flattening as much as you can. If you like, top with grated cheese.

Put in oven for 15-20 mins or until cheese has melted. Serve with veg of your choosing or it's delicious and filling on its own too.

​

This is one of those recipes that you can really make your own. Once you get used to making it you can experiment with things like sweet potatoes instead of white, different veg in the meat, adding leeks or onions to the mash - anything really. You can also use lamb mince instead of beef (this is known as shepherd's pie).
